text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- President Hosni Mubarak said told media people that Egypt's concern was to achieve comprehensive and just peace in the region. In conjunction with the United States and all the parties concerned, it is trying to move the peace process forward because the alternative to peace is very grave.
- Prime Minister Kamal Ganzouri holds a meeting with four ministers today to discuss the performance of the investment offices in the provinces.

- President Hosni Mubarak, at the meeting with media people, said Egypt was not negotiating on behalf of the Palestinians. Egypt is trying to push the peace process forward but in the end the decision is the Palestinians'. He said the aim of his meeting with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in Sharm el-Sheikh was to break the deadlock in the peace process.

- Mubarak said that presidential adviser Osama el-Baz would travel to Israel today to find out Netanyahu's opinion on the Palestinian proposals Baz conveyed to him after his meeting with Palestinian President Yasser Arafat.

- Mubarak said the census last year showed that the population of Egypt was 61.5 million and that the rate of growth has slowed from three percent a year to 2.1 percent, despite a decline in infant mortality.

- Libyan leader Muammar Gaddafi has given his government instructions to give Egyptian companies preferential treatment in foreign tenders for goods. This was announced by Industry and Mining Secretary (minister) Muftah Azzouz.

- Mubarak told media people that Egypt's role was to bridge the gap between points of view to bring about comprehensive and just peace. "There are more serious problems than Abu Ghneim," he said. He also said the government was encouraging small businessmen, to create jobs.

- Mubarak said the children of Egyptian women married to foreigners were entitled to free education and permanent residence in Egypt. They may also work in Egypt but not in government agencies and establishments.
- The joint Egyptian-Libyan coordination committee discussed trade, especially in iron and steel, fertilisers and chemicals.
